evidence.claim: Route 47 runs 61.09 miles between Pamplin City and South Hill, with its entire length designated a Virginia Byway.
evidence.quote: The state highway runs 61.09 miles (98.31 km) from U.S. Route 1 (US 1) and US 58 Business in South Hill north to US 460 Business in Pamplin City, Virginia.

evidence.claim: Near Pamplin, it parallels a railway and follows the boundary between Charlotte and Prince Edward counties.
evidence.quote: The state highway has brief stretches entirely within one of the counties before continuing to serve as the county line as the highway closely parallels Norfolk Southern's Blue Ridge District.

evidence.claim: Farther south, the highway follows the drainage divide between the Meherrin River to the north and the Roanoke to the south.
evidence.quote: on top of the drainage divide between the Meherrin River to the north and the Roanoke River to the south.

evidence.claim: At the northern end, Pamplin was a stop on the Southside Railroad in the mid-19th century.
evidence.quote: This town was a stop on the Southside Railroad in the mid-19th century.

evidence.claim: The rail corridor from Burkeville to Pamplin later became High Bridge Trail State Park, and an extension into town opened in April 2024.
evidence.quote: The rail line from Burkeville to Pamplin City was converted by Virginia Department of Parks and Recreation into High Bridge Trail State Park.

evidence.claim: For a southbound drive, leave US 460 Business at Pamplin and follow Route 47 toward Cullen and Charlotte Court House.
evidence.quote: SR 47 exits Charlotte Court House as Thomas Jefferson Highway. The highway crosses over Norfolk Southern Railway's Altavista District rail line at the hamlet of Cullen.

evidence.claim: Beyond the county seat, cross Roanoke Creek and continue through Drakes Branch to Craftons Gate.
evidence.quote: SR 47 leaves the town as Tollhouse Highway and crosses Roanoke Creek before reaching Charlotte Court House.

evidence.claim: Chase City brings the route onto Main Street and Second Street, then the road follows the divide through Wightman to South Hill’s Atlantic Street.
evidence.quote: SR 47 enters the town of Chase City as Second Street. In the center of town, Second Street intersects Main Street.

evidence.claim: Its brick, temple-form design became a model for Virginia court buildings in the 1830s and 1840s.

evidence.claim: Patrick Henry’s last political speech came earlier, in March 1799, at Charlotte Courthouse, when he opposed the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions.
evidence.quote: Patrick Henry gave his last political speech in opposition to the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions at Charlotte Courthouse in March 1799.

evidence.claim: The present building therefore postdates that speech.
evidence.quote: It was built in 1821–1823

evidence.claim: Chase City’s former high school has become housing, while its brick Colonial Revival buildings remain part of the town’s architecture.
evidence.quote: It consists of two two-story, brick Colonial Revival-style buildings connected by a one-story connector building built in 1960.

evidence.claim: The school building was erected in 1908 and expanded in 1917.
evidence.quote: The school building was built in 1908 and expanded in 1917.

evidence.claim: It closed in 1980; in 1991 the complex was rehabilitated as apartments for elderly residents.

evidence.claim: A separate brick building constructed for vocational agriculture classes in 1917 also belongs to the complex.

evidence.claim: The town itself was incorporated in 1873 and named for Salmon P. Chase, Lincoln’s treasury secretary and a United States chief justice.
evidence.quote: Chase City was incorporated in 1873 and named for Salmon P. Chase, United States Chief Justice and Lincoln's Secretary of the Treasury.
